There are convenient functions that allow you to change the shooting mode with just one touch if registered to the camera in advance.

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture the night parade in vivid colors. The camera sets the shutter speed to minimize subject blur and uses a continuous release mode, so select the best shot from the sequence.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To focus on a desired position: · Tap the focus area on the monitor. ■When the camera has trouble focusing: · Use an AF-area mode with a wider focus area like [Wide-area AF (S)] and [Wide-area AF (L)]. ■If the subject is too dark: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the subject is too bright: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■To make “Noise” (in the form of randomly-spaced bright pixels) less noticeable: · Set the maximum ISO sensitivity value to ISO [3200] or below."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture food with natural-looking colors and brightness with blurred background and surroundings.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■When the camera has trouble focusing (the focus point not displayed in green): · Move away from the subject (the camera cannot focus if it is closer than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). · Use an AF-area mode with a smaller focus area like [Single-point AF], [Wide-area AF (S)], and [Wide-area AF (L)]. ■If the subject is too dark: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the subject is too bright: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■To make the color of the photo more blue: · Set the White balance to [Incandescent]. ■To make the color of the photo more red: · Set the White balance to [Cloudy] or [Shade]. ■To blur the background: · Shoot with reduced depth of field. · Shooting tips to use a reduced depth of field: 1) Get closer to the subject (Note to be further away than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). 2) Use a lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). 3) Use a telephoto lens or zoom in a zoom lens."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture food with natural-looking colors and brightness and keep the entire dish in focus.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■When the camera has trouble focusing (the focus point not displayed in green): · Move away from the subject (the camera cannot focus if it is closer than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). · Use an AF-area mode with a smaller focus area like [Single-point AF], [Wide-area AF (S)], and [Wide-area AF (L)]. ■If the subject is too dark: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the subject is too bright: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■To make the color of the photo more blue: · Set the White balance to [Incandescent]. ■To make the color of the photo more red: · Set the White balance to [Cloudy] or [Shade]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture items for auction with high contrast, vivid colors, and overall sharp focus.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To blur the background and take a crisp shot of the product: · Use [Small objects]. ■To minimize camera blur: · Use a tripod, a table, or other means to fix the camera, or hold the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■When the camera has trouble focusing (the focus point not displayed in green): · Move away from the subject (the camera cannot focus if it is closer than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). ■To take a clear shot of both the product and its background: · Set a smaller (narrower) aperture such as f/11. ■To take pictures that make the subject stand out: · Adjust how natural light hits the subject or change the direction of spotlights so that the subject is illuminated to your liking."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture the redness of the evening scenery. Autofocus is set to make it easier to focus even in dark environments.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To minimize camera blur: · Use a tripod, a table, or a fence to fix the camera, or hold the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■If the scenery appears brighter in the image than it does to the eye: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■If the scenery appears darker in the image than it does to the eye: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■To emphasize the redness of the sunset: · Set the White balance to [Cloudy] or [Shade]. ■To preserve details in highlights and shadows in high-contrast scenes: · Set Active D-Lighting to [Extra high]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take pictures of landscapes such as mountains and forests with natural tones and colors.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To focus on a desired position: · Tap the area to be focused on the monitor. ■To preserve details in highlights and shadows in high-contrast scenes: · Set Active D-Lighting to [Extra high]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture night scenes with clear, vivid colors.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To minimize camera blur: · Use a tripod, a table, or a fence to fix the camera, or hold the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To focus on a desired position: · Tap the area to be focused on the monitor. · Position the camera’s focus point on the area to be focused and press the shutter-release button halfway to lock the focus. While keeping the button pressed, recompose the photograph and shoot. ■When the camera has trouble focusing: · Use an AF-area mode with a wider focus area like [Wide-area AF (S)] and [Wide-area AF (L)]. · At a location with contrast, press the shutter-release button halfway to lock the focus, then change the composition and shoot. · Focus manually. ■When the subject is too bright: · While viewing the display, adjust the exposure to your liking by selecting a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■To make “Noise” less noticeable: · Fix the camera on a tripod or other means and set ISO sensitivity to ISO [400] or below. ■To make the color of the photo more blue: · Set the White balance to [Incandescent]. ■To make the color of the photo more red: · Set the White balance to [Cloudy] or [Shade]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take balanced photos of portrait subjects and night scenery with a night view in the background. Autofocus is set to make it easier to focus in dark environments.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To take pictures in focus and minimize subject blur: · Use a flash or LED light or move to a location by streetlights to shine the subject’s face. · In low-light conditions, use a tripod or fix the camera on a flat surface like a table.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To reduce noise: · Fix the camera on a tripod or a flat surface like a table and select ISO [3200] or below for [ISO sensitivity settings] > [Maximum sensitivity]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture pets with natural-looking colors. Shoot the best moment as the camera adjusts focus continuously in response to the subject’s motion and takes bursts in the continuous low-speed release mode. The background can be either blurred or in focus.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To capture the best expression of your pet: · Hold the camera at a low angle to your pet’s eye level.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To keep the subject in focus: · Pointing the camera at the subjects and pressing the shutter-release button halfway will display yellow borders on the faces or eyes and locks the focus on the subject. ■To capture the best moment: · Prepare for the sudden movement of the subject during shooting by positioning the focus point over the subject and pressing and holding the shutter-release button to let the camera start a low-speed burst to capture the moment. ■To blur the background: · Shoot with reduced depth of field. · Shooting tips to use a reduced depth of field: 1) Get closer to the subject (Note to be further away than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). 2) Use a lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). 3) Use a telephoto lens or zoom in a zoom lens."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take clear pictures of fast-moving pets with fast shutter speeds to minimize subject blur. Capture even the slightest movement of active pets as the camera adjusts focus continuously in response to the subject’s motion and takes bursts in the continuous high-speed release mode.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To keep the subject in focus: · Pointing the camera at the subjects and pressing the shutter-release button halfway will display yellow borders on the faces or eyes and locks the focus on the subject. ■When the subject causes motion blur: · Select S for the shooting (exposure) mode and set faster shutter speeds (for example, [1/2000 s]). ■To capture a moment of agile motion: · Position the focus point over the actively moving subject and press and hold the shutter-release button to let the camera start a high-speed burst to capture the moment."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take vivid pictures of flowers. The background can be blurred or clear so that the surrounding flowers are also in focus.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To focus on a desired position: · Tap the area to be focused on the monitor. ■When the camera has trouble focusing: · Use an AF-area mode with a wider focus area like [Single-point AF], [Wide-area AF (S)], and [Wide-area AF (L)]. · At a location with contrast, press the shutter-release button halfway to lock the focus, then change the composition and shoot. · Focus manually. ■To blur the background: · Shoot with reduced depth of field. · Shooting tips to use a reduced depth of field: 1) Get closer to the subject (Note to be further away than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). 2) Use a lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). 3) Use a telephoto lens or zoom in a zoom lens. ■To take close-up photos of flowers: · Using a macro lens makes it easier to focus on nearby subjects, allowing capture of enlarged photographs with fine details. · Using a telephoto lens or zooming in a zoom lens lets you take close-up photos of flowers with a blurred background without getting too close. ■If the scenery appears darker in the image than it appears to the eye: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the scenery appears in the image brighter than it appears to the eye: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take portrait pictures with a soft complexion and natural look. The background can be blurred or in focus.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To keep the portrait subjects in focus: · Pointing the camera at the subjects and pressing the shutter-release button halfway will display yellow borders on the faces or eyes to lock the focus. ■To blur the background: · Shoot with reduced depth of field. · Shooting tips for reduced depth of field: 1) Get closer to the subject (further away than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). 2) Use a lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). 3) Use a telephoto lens or zoom in a zoom lens."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take naturally-colored portrait pictures with their backgrounds. The background can be either blurred or in focus.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To avoid eye-closing shots: · View the picture to see if anyone closed their eyes. · Select a continuous release mode, then press and hold the shutter-release button to shoot multiple photos.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■Keep the portrait subjects in focus: · Pointing the camera at the subjects and pressing the shutter-release button halfway will display yellow borders on the faces or eyes to lock the focus."

"---Mode Introduction--- Prevent the portrait subject from appearing dark in scenes where the brightness differs between the subject and the background due to backlighting or other reasons.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■If the portrait subject appears too dark: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the portrait subject appears too bright: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■If the image appears grainy (for example, when the ISO sensitivity is high): · Set Active D-Lighting to [Normal] or [Low]."

"---Mode Introduction--- Freeze the motion of water in a river or waterfall, or the movement of water droplets, or capture the trail of flowing water.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To minimize camera blur: · To capture the trail of flowing water, use a tripod, a table, or a fence to fix the camera, or holding the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To freeze the motion of fast-flowing water: · Select the [“Freeze” motion] option and set faster shutter speeds (for example, [1/250 s] or [1/500 s]). ■To capture longer trail of flowing water: · Select the [Create long motion trails] option and set slower shutter speeds (for example, [2 s] or [4 s]; use of a tripod is recommended)."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take self-portrait pictures that include the background naturally. The background can be blurred or in focus.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To take pictures with a good eye contact: · When taking a picture, look at the center of the lens instead of the center of the monitor display facing you. ■To clearly show background scenery and surrounding environment: · Use a wide-angle lens or zoom out with a zoom lens to include a wider angle of view, making it easier to show the background and surrounding environment.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To keep the portrait subjects in focus: · Pointing the camera at the subjects and pressing the shutter-release button halfway will display yellow borders on the faces or eyes and lock the focus."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture handmade items or decorative objects with high contrast, vivid colors, with the background blurred.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To take pictures that make the subject stand out: · Adjust how natural light hits the subject or change the direction of spotlights so that the subject is illuminated to your liking. ■To take a clear shot of both the product and its background: · Use [Online auctions]. ■To minimize camera blur: · Use a tripod, a table, or other means to fix the camera, or hold the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■When the camera has trouble focusing (the focus point not displayed in green): · Move away from the subject (the camera cannot focus if it is closer than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). ■To blur the background: · Shoot with reduced depth of field. · Shooting tips to use a reduced depth of field: 1) Get closer to the subject (Note to be further away than the minimum focus distance indicated on the lens). 2) Use a lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). 3) Use a telephoto lens or zoom in a zoom lens. ■To take close-up photos of the subject: · Using a macro lens makes it easier to focus on nearby subjects, allowing for enlarged photographs with clear and fine details. · Using a telephoto lens or zooming in a zoom lens lets you take close-up photos of the subject with a blurred background without getting too close."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take pictures of subjects playing sports indoors with natural-looking colors. Increase ISO sensitivity and set a fast shutter speed to avoid motion blur. Capture even the slightest movement by operating the camera in bursts and adjust the focus continuously in response to the subject’s motion.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To take impressive shots: · Use a telephoto lens (for example, focal length of 200 mm).
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■For dark indoor environments: · Select a higher ISO sensitivity value. ■To capture the motion of a portrait subject: · While tracking the subject, press and hold the shutter-release button to take bursts. · Hold the camera in the composition of your choice, and when the subject comes into view, press and hold the shutter-release button to take bursts. ■When the subject causes motion blur: · Select S for the shooting (exposure) mode and set faster shutter speeds (for example, [1/2000 s])."

"---Mode Introduction--- Shoot at the best moment by operating the camera in bursts and adjusting the focus continuously in response to the movement of the portrait subject. Capture the flow of the movement or freeze motion of portrait subjects playing sports outdoors.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To take impressive shots: · Use a telephoto lens (for example, focal length of 200 mm).
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To capture the motion of a portrait subject: · While tracking the subject, press and hold the shutter-release button to take bursts. · Hold the camera in the composition of your choice, and when the subject comes into the view, press and hold the shutter-release button to take bursts. ■For smoother focus: · Focus in advance on the position close to where the subject will come into frame. ■When the subject causes motion blur: · Select faster shutter speeds (for example, [1/2000 s])."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture the starry sky. The camera sets the shutter speed to open the shutter for a set period.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To minimize camera blur: · Fix the camera on a tripod and take pictures with the self-timer. ■To include the surrounding scenery in starry sky photos: · Use a wide-angle lens or zoom out a zoom lens.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■To make “Noise” (in the form of randomly-spaced bright pixels) less noticeable: · Use a fast prime lens with a small maximum aperture value (minimum f-number). ■If the subject is too dark: · Set high ISO sensitivity value (for example, ISO [6400] or above). ■If the subject is too bright: · Set low ISO sensitivity value (for example, ISO [400] or below)."

"---Mode Introduction--- Take photos of architecture and cityscapes with balanced tones and colors.
---Shooting Techniques--- ■To minimize camera blur: · Use a tripod, a table, or a fence to fix the camera, or hold the camera firmly by bringing your elbows in against the sides of your chest. · Turn [Vibration reduction] off when the camera is fixed by a tripod or other means. ■To take pictures of buildings and cityscapes with a wide angle of view: · Use a wide-angle lens or zoom out a zoom lens."

"---Mode Introduction--- Capture beautiful cherry blossoms in natural colors.
---Camera Operation Tips--- ■When the camera has trouble focusing (the focus point not displayed in green): · Use an AF-area mode with a smaller focus area like [Single-point AF], [Wide-area AF (S)], and [Wide-area AF (L)]. ■If the subject is too dark: · Select a higher (more positive) value for exposure compensation. ■If the subject is too bright: · Select a lower (more negative) value for exposure compensation. ■To capture vivid colors: · Set Picture Control to [Landscape] or [Vivid]."
